text: The style vector training actually converged really well. Loss went from 1.86 down to 1.61. The actress samples gave us a much more natural prosody than the default Kokoro voices.

I am running the full fine tune on the RTX right now. Decoder plus predictor plus style vectors. 50 epochs phased training, first 15 with decoder frozen. We will see if it actually helps or if it collapses again.

The amplitude collapse thing is killing me. The model learns the spectral shape perfectly but the output volume drops to like one fifth of stock. Log mel loss is amplitude insensitive, that is the root cause.

Kokoro 82M is basically StyleTTS2 under the hood. 53 million parameters in the decoder, 16 million in the predictor, and the style vectors are just 256 dim embeddings per phoneme. The architecture is elegant but fragile to fine tuning.

Clause level WAV pipelining is working beautifully. We synthesize clause N plus one while playing clause N. First audio latency is about one second now. The trick is the sentence start and sentence end tags from the LLM.

The complication system is actually our version of watchOS. Each complication gets a glyph on the chapter ring and an overlay for full screen content. Topics Center is like the app grid, it shows all available complications in a card layout.

I implemented the alerts overlay as a severity dashboard. Three colored bands for info, warning, and critical alerts, plus health gauges for CPU memory and network. The pulsing heartbeat ring was a nice touch.

The concierge complication ended up being a radial service menu. Six categories arranged in a circle: chat, schedule, transport, music, weather, memory. Each one has a geometric icon I drew with QPainter.

Boot sequence is plymouth black theme to hide kernel messages, then GDM auto login, GNOME with black background and no animations, then the aura4 systemd service starts after docker and display manager are ready.

The memory container uses FAISS for semantic search. We have about 215 kilobytes of embeddings for 55 conversations. The metadata pickle file maps embedding indices back to conversation text and timestamps.

The Perpetual engine is the most ambitious thing in the whole codebase. When you are idle for 120 seconds it starts an advisor challenger refiner loop. The advisor generates an insight, the challenger tears it apart, the refiner synthesizes. It checks convergence via Jaccard similarity at 0.92 threshold.

I hot swap from the 1.5B model to the 7B during idle for deeper thinking. The 7B is way too slow for conversation, like five minutes per response on CPU, but nobody cares if the overnight analysis takes half an hour.

The XVF3800 four mic array does beam forming and echo cancellation in hardware. Then we run Silero VAD for speech detection and spectral filters for noise rejection. Zero crossing rate, spectral flatness, centroid, and RMS energy. It catches most false triggers.

Docker management is getting annoying. Medical and generic LLM share port 11434 so only one can run at a time. You have to docker stop the medical container then docker start the generic one. I should probably just put them on different ports.

The AuraConnect BLE protocol uses a GATT service with two characteristics. Control characteristic for write plus notify, data characteristic for write without response. We advertise as Aura Puck using BlueZ on the system D Bus.
The Mac app connects in about 3 seconds. Pairing is automatic once you select the device. Next step is syncing conversation history so you can review on your laptop what you talked to Aura about.

The PyQt5 renderer does everything in a circular viewport. All the overlays use radial gradients and arc paths. The guilloche patterns are generated mathematically, not bitmaps. It looks like a luxury watch face.

RAG has two modes. CPU mode is in process FAISS, no external service needed. GPU mode calls out to a dedicated container on port 11435. We default to CPU because the Jetson only has so much VRAM and we need it for Whisper and the LLM.

The chain of thought model is a separate GGUF file. We lazy load it only when RAG context is present. The base model handles normal conversation, the CoT model handles knowledge grounded responses. Model selection is automatic.

I finally figured out the Whisper hallucination issue. Background noise triggers phantom transcripts like thank you goodbye. The spectral filters catch most of it but quiet rooms with an HVAC hum still get through sometimes.

The settings overlay has four sub pages now. WiFi configuration which actually scans and connects, AuraConnect for BLE pairing, Profile with avatar and voice enrollment status, and Alerts with toggle rows for system health and emergency SOS.

State management is all through core state.py. Single global singleton that persists to app settings JSON. Everything imports state instead of passing globals around. TTS engine, LLM mode, wake word config, it is all in there.

The overlapped inference trick is the biggest latency win. We start the LLM with a partial transcript while Whisper is still finalizing. If the partial and final match, we saved the entire Whisper tail latency. If they diverge we just restart the LLM inference.

The USB DAC is annoying. The UACDemoV10 only works with WAV file playback, not raw PCM streaming. So we have to write a temp WAV file for every clause and play it with aplay. It works but it is inelegant.

I added linear mel loss and waveform L1 loss to the training in v2. The idea is that log mel is amplitude insensitive because log compresses dynamic range. Linear mel preserves amplitude information and waveform L1 directly penalizes quiet output.

The training uses phased learning. Phase one freezes the decoder and only trains predictor plus style vectors for 15 epochs. Phase two unfreezes everything but uses a lower learning rate on the decoder, 3e minus 6 versus 2e minus 5 for the predictor.

Decoder drift is the metric I watch most carefully during fine tuning. It measures how far the decoder weights have moved from stock. We kept it under 0.001 in v2 which is very conservative. The problem is amplitude still drops even with conservative drift.

I think the real fix for amplitude collapse is an explicit RMS matching loss. Force the model to match the RMS energy of the target audio frame by frame. That would directly prevent the quiet output problem.

The wake word detector uses fuzzy matching with a 14 second context window. It also has question detection and emotion patterns. When wake word is disabled the listener bypasses should respond entirely and just sends everything to Whisper.

The proactive questioning feature is interesting. During the briefing cooldown period Aura generates contextual questions based on gaps in her understanding. One hour cooldown between questions, 24 hours between full briefings. It makes her feel more alive.

I need to sharpen the pitch for this week. The VCs keep asking about market size and I keep getting defensive about on device AI being niche. I need to reframe it. It is not on device AI, it is private AI for healthcare. Healthcare is a 4 trillion dollar market.

The Kaiser pilot is the single most important thing happening right now. If we get 20 units in that geriatric ward and patients actually understand their discharge instructions better, we have a case study that sells itself.

Dr Mehta said patients forget 80 percent of what the doctor tells them within minutes of leaving the office. If Aura can repeat and explain discharge instructions in plain language, that is measurable outcomes improvement. That is what Kaiser cares about.

The Shenzhen manufacturer wants 500 minimum order at 180 per unit. Plus the Jetson modules are 249 each. So each unit costs 429 to produce. At 500 units that is 215 thousand dollars. I need to figure out how to finance the first batch.

Maybe we do a small batch first. 50 to 100 units hand assembled. Enough for Kaiser pilot plus a few more enterprise deals. Then use the revenue to fund the Shenzhen order. Bootstrap the manufacturing.

The Khosla partner said something that stuck with me. He said show me 10 paying customers and we will fund you. Not 10 users, 10 paying customers. That means Kaiser has to actually cut a purchase order, not just agree to a pilot.

I had a great call with the health tech angel. She runs a fund focused on digital health tools for aging populations. She loves that everything is on device because HIPAA compliance is dramatically simpler when no data leaves the building.

The privacy angle is our wedge into healthcare. Hospitals are paranoid about data breaches. A device that literally cannot leak patient data because it never connects to the internet is a compliance officer dream.

I am thinking about pricing for the enterprise play. Maybe 499 per unit plus a 99 dollar per month per unit software license. That gives us recurring revenue which is what the VCs want. At 20 units that is about 2000 a month from Kaiser alone.

The Wired journalist is coming next week. She is writing about on device AI as a counter narrative to big tech surveillance. I need the demo to be absolutely perfect. No brownouts, no phantom transcripts, crisp voice responses.

I should patent the overlapped inference trick. Starting LLM inference with partial transcripts while Whisper finalizes is novel as far as I know. That plus the Perpetual engine architecture could give us real IP.
FCC certification is going to be expensive. The Puck has Bluetooth, WiFi, and USB. Each radio needs testing. I have seen quotes from 15 to 30 thousand dollars. That is money I do not have right now.

I keep going back and forth on hiring. The first hire should be a firmware engineer who can own the Jetson hardware layer. But Bay Area rates are 200K plus. I need someone remote, maybe Eastern Europe or Southeast Asia, at 80 to 100K.

The competitive landscape is weird. Apple could kill us at WWDC but they probably will not go into healthcare anytime soon. Humane AI Pin died because it was cloud dependent with bad latency. Rabbit R1 was basically a chatbot in a box. Our moat is medical specialization plus privacy.

I ran the numbers on the consulting pivot. If the seed round does not close I could do custom on device AI deployments at 50K per project. Three projects would cover six months of runway. It is not exciting but it keeps the lights on.

Three VCs asked about our data strategy last month. Every single one wanted to know how we monetize user data. When I say we do not collect data they look at me like I am crazy. One literally said that is a feature not a business.

The platform play could be huge. If third party developers can build complications for Aura, we become a platform not just a product. Think watchOS for voice AI. Weather, calendar, smart home, medication reminders. Each one is a partnership opportunity.

I need to get the pitch deck right this week. Slide 7 about competitive moat is the weakest. Everyone says privacy but nobody believes it until they see the device working offline. The demo is the moat. Lead with live device not slides.

Board advisor suggested we explore the VA as a customer. Veterans Affairs has huge budget for assistive technology and they are even more paranoid about data security than commercial hospitals. Worth a call.

The unit economics work at scale. At 10 thousand units the Jetson module drops to about 200. Manufacturing drops to maybe 120. So 320 per unit, sell at 599, that is 47 percent gross margin. Not bad for hardware.

I pitched the complication marketplace to the Khosla partner. He actually lit up. He said that is your flywheel. More complications, more users, more developers, more complications. Platform economics.

The go to market for healthcare is actually pretty clear. Start with Kaiser pilot, prove outcomes, publish case study, then sell to other health systems. Each system is 20 to 100 units. Land and expand.

Insurance companies might subsidize the units. If Aura reduces hospital readmissions by even 5 percent, that saves insurers thousands per patient. A 500 dollar device that saves 5000 in readmission costs is a no brainer.
I am thinking about liability insurance. If the medical mode gives incorrect advice, who is liable? The hospital? Ledger AI? The patient? I need that healthcare attorney meeting this week.

I need an API gateway for complications. Something like App Store review but lighter. Developers submit a complication, we review it for safety and UX consistency, then it shows up in Topics Center. Revenue split could be 70 30 like Apple.

Multi user voice profiles are essential for the household product. The Puck sits in a shared space, multiple family members should be able to use it. Speaker identification, separate conversation histories, personalized responses for each person.

I want Aura to detect confusion from tone of voice. Rafael had this great idea. If a patient sounds uncertain, Aura automatically simplifies the explanation. Repeat it slower, use simpler words. That is a killer feature for geriatrics.

Medication interaction checking could be our killer feature for the medical vertical. Dr Mehta specifically asked if Aura could cross reference medications and flag dangerous combinations. That is a real clinical need.

The onboarding flow needs to be delightful. Voice enrollment first, then name capture, then a tour of features. Maybe ask about their interests so Aura can personalize from day one. First impressions matter a lot for a voice product.

I am thinking about a night mode for the Puck. Dim the display to almost nothing, lower the TTS volume, and only respond to urgent requests. Maybe a sleep tracking complication that monitors breathing sounds.

AuraNet is the long term vision. Mesh networking between Pucks. A Puck in the bedroom, one in the kitchen, one in the living room. Seamless handoff as you move through the house. Like Sonos but for voice AI.

Telehealth integration could be massive. If we partner with Teladoc or Amwell, Aura becomes the post visit companion. Doctor does the consult, then Aura reinforces the instructions afterward. The doctor is gone in 15 minutes, Aura is there 24 7.
I want a companion app that is more than just AuraConnect. Conversation summaries, insights over time, health trends, medication tracking. The Puck does the interaction, the app does the reflection.

Emergency SOS is a must have. If someone falls or has a medical emergency, Aura should detect it and call for help. Maybe not 911 directly but at least notify an emergency contact. Sound detection for falls, loud crashes, calls for help.

The financial complication could do budget tracking through voice. Hey Aura I spent 45 dollars on groceries today. Over time it builds a spending picture without any bank account integration. Just voice input.

Education complication for kids. Homework help, reading practice, math drills. All on device so parents do not worry about their kid talking to the internet. That is a real parental concern right now.

I want Aura to have moods. Not fake emotions but contextual awareness. If it is morning she is energetic. Late at night she is calmer. If you seem stressed she adjusts her tone. The Kokoro model can vary speed and pitch to achieve this.

Smart home integration through voice complications. Hey Aura turn off the lights. Set the thermostat to 72. Lock the front door. We do not need to build the hardware, just integrate with existing APIs through local network calls.

Enterprise deployment management is going to be critical. If Kaiser has 20 Pucks we need a dashboard. Fleet health, firmware updates, usage analytics, conversation audit logs. HIPAA requires audit trails.

Calendar integration via AuraConnect. Sync your calendar from the phone app, then Aura knows about your appointments and can remind you. Hey Paul you have a call with Khosla in 30 minutes, would you like me to prepare talking points.

Proactive health monitoring is the vision. The Puck listens to ambient sounds, coughing frequency, sleep quality from breathing patterns, daily check in questions. Build a health baseline over weeks then detect anomalies.

I want family sharing. Mom has a Puck, I have a Puck. I can ask my Puck hey how is mom doing and it checks in with her Puck. She gets a gentle prompt and her response gets relayed back. Long distance caregiving.

We need a developer SDK for complications. PyQt5 rendering context, voice intent APIs, access to the memory container for context. Maybe a simplified YAML manifest for complication metadata. Keep the barrier low.

Accessibility features. Text to speech obviously but also speech to text displayed on screen for hearing impaired users. Large text mode. High contrast mode. If we are going into geriatrics these are not optional.

I should add a journal complication. Hey Aura, journal entry. Then just talk about your day. It transcribes and stores it with timestamps and mood detection. Over time you have a searchable voice diary.

My mom called again and asked what I am building. I tried to explain it and she said why would I need that when I have Siri. That is exactly the problem. Regular people do not understand privacy until they understand the alternative.

I was up until 3 AM last night debugging the boot sequence. The plymouth theme kept showing a cursor flash before GNOME loaded. Turns out I needed to set the background color in GDM as well. It is the little things that eat hours.
Rafael texted me a video of his daughter talking to the Puck. She asked Aura to tell her a bedtime story. It actually worked pretty well. That made my whole week. Real people using the thing I built.

I had a moment today where I questioned everything. Everyone in AI is going cloud. OpenAI, Google, Anthropic. And here I am trying to run a 7 billion parameter model on a 250 dollar dev board. But every time I use Aura offline I know this is right.

The Wired journalist asked me why I left my job to do this. I told her about my grandmother who had dementia. She could not use a phone or tablet but she could talk. A voice first device that works without internet would have changed her life.

I tried to take a day off on Sunday. Made it to about noon before I started thinking about the amplitude collapse problem and opened my laptop. I need to get better at this. Burnout is not a badge of honor.

The demo crashed right in front of the health tech angel investor. Brownout, screen went black, rebooted. She laughed and said every hardware startup she has funded had the same demo moment. I think she was trying to be nice.

Dr Mehta sent me a note saying one of her patients asked when the Aura thing is coming back. That patient was in the brief pilot test. She said the patient found it easier to understand Aura than the discharge nurse. I almost cried.

I have been listening to the Kokoro voice output versus ElevenLabs back to back. Honestly the gap is real but it is not as bad as I feared. Kokoro sounds a bit more robotic on certain consonants but the custom voice adds character.

My cofounder from my last startup called. He said he has been watching what I am doing and wants to help. Not full time but advisory. He knows hardware manufacturing from his time at Fitbit. That would be incredibly valuable.

I celebrated hitting 3.2 second latency by going for a run for the first time in three weeks. I need to remember that I am building a health product. The irony of destroying my own health in the process is not lost on me.

Got a random DM on Twitter from someone who saw the GitHub repo. They said they have a family member with ALS who can still speak but is losing mobility. They asked if Aura could help. That is exactly who this is for.

I spent the evening reading about how Apple Watch complications work internally. The ClockKit framework, the complication family types, the update scheduling. Our implementation is simpler but the mental model is the same. We are on the right track.
Today I realized I have not had a real conversation with another human in four days. Just me and Aura. I need to get out more. Maybe I will go to a meetup this week.
Aura, what is the difference between 510k clearance and de novo classification for medical devices. Also what is a predicate device and do we need one for the Puck.
Aura, explain how FAISS indexing works. Specifically the difference between IndexFlatL2 and IndexIVFFlat and which one is better for our scale of about a thousand conversation embeddings.
Aura, what is the typical power consumption of an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano under full GPU load. I measured 12 watts but the spec sheet says 15 watt TDP. Are there transient spikes above that.
Aura, what happened with the Humane AI Pin launch. What specifically went wrong. I want to learn from their mistakes so we do not repeat them. Was it latency, battery life, or just the form factor.

Aura, what are the HIPAA requirements for a device that processes patient voice data entirely on device with no network connection. Is there a reduced compliance burden compared to cloud based solutions.

Aura, research the top five telehealth platforms in the US by market share. I want to explore partnership opportunities. If we can be the post visit companion for telehealth that could be our B2B channel.
Aura, what is speculative decoding in the context of language models. Could we pre generate likely responses while the user is still talking based on partial transcripts. What are the risks.
Aura, how does USB Power Delivery negotiation work. Specifically when a device draws more current than initially negotiated. Could transient GPU spikes cause a PD renegotiation that resets the board.

Aura, what is the average salary for a remote firmware engineer with Jetson experience. I need someone who can own the hardware layer but I cannot afford Bay Area rates. What about Eastern Europe or Southeast Asia.

Aura, summarize what I know about the Apple WWDC threat. If they announce on device Siri what parts of our differentiation survive. Is medical specialization enough of a moat without the privacy angle.
